# GEO report: orchard-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 98/100, Strong

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 22.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 98. High = (22.5 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 98.

This is a small Next.js App Router site with four routes: `/`, `/varieties`, `/visit` and `/account`. Everything I read follows the rules except one missing meta description on a page that is already hidden from search. Nothing was left as "Can't tell", so the score is a single number. It is read from code only.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Add a description to the account page (optional, low stakes)
- **Why it matters:** Every route should have a title and a description. This page is deliberately hidden from search (`noindex`), so the practical effect is small.
- **Where:** `app/account/page.tsx:1`
- **What the code says:** `export const metadata = { title: 'Your account', robots: { index: false, follow: false } };`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 100/100 (GEO-012 earns its full 2 points, 24 ÷ 23 capped at 23 ÷ 23).

### 2. Confirm real crawlers get through your CDN or firewall
- **Why it matters:** Code can't show whether bot protection in front of the site blocks the crawlers `robots.txt` welcomes.
- **Where:** outside the repository.
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: *` / `Allow: /` (`public/robots.txt:1-2`)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** the code score stays at 98. This confirms real-world access, which the score doesn't cover.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and a sensible size | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`, plain text, valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2` allows all; only `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot` (training) are blocked, matching `trainingCrawlers: "block"` |
| GEO-014 | Sitemap-listed and linked routes are indexable | Clear | Not run | `/`, `/varieties` and `/visit` have no `noindex`. `/account` is `noindex` but isn't in the sitemap or nav |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on the declared origin | Clear | Not run | `app/page.tsx:1`, `app/varieties/page.tsx:1`, `app/visit/page.tsx:1` (3 of 3 indexable routes) |
| GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Clear | Not run | All pages are Server Components with static text and no `'use client'` |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | A valid sitemap that robots.txt points to | Clear | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml` is a valid urlset; `public/robots.txt:11` has an absolute `Sitemap:` line |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` are present | Problem | Not run | `app/account/page.tsx:1` has no description (3 of 4 routes clear, so 1.5 of 2 points). `lang="en"` is at `app/layout.tsx:5` |
| GEO-016 | Key routes are reachable through plain links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:7` uses `<a href>` for all three public routes |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with the AI-search policy | Clear | Not run | Only a scoped `data-nosnippet` at `app/layout.tsx:9`. No page-wide `nosnippet`, and no middleware or `headers()` in the tracked files |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | Not run | Layout and 4 pages read: no images, links have text, every page has a title |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | `llms.txt` (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | No `llms.txt` present. This is never scored or recommended |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app |

## Can't tell from code

- **Live status codes and headers (GEO-013, GEO-014, GEO-017):** code can't show real status codes, redirects, or `X-Robots-Tag` headers set by a host or CDN. A live scan would confirm these.
- **Canonical targets (GEO-015):** whether each canonical URL really answers 200 is live only.
- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools and search engines to find the public pages, as `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` in `geo.config.json` says.
- `https://www.orchard.example` from `geo.config.json` is the real origin.
- Blocking `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot` is deliberate, per `trainingCrawlers: "block"`. I didn't count it either way.
- Bash was denied partway through. I used the tracked-file list from my first command and the Read tool. I didn't look for untracked files such as `next.config` or middleware, so header-based rules rest on the tracked files only.

## Outside GEO

None noticed.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-012`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
